about: Grace Tyler Estate Winery is Richard and Elizabeth Hamilton’s farm winery on the north shore of Oneida Lake in Constantia. They bought the land in 2012, harvested their first grapes in 2017 and opened in 2018. Their tasting room is built from aspen cut on the site, it is open year-round and can be reached by snowmobile trail. They grow and work with grapes that can survive Oswego County winters.

Baco Noir is one of the oldest of those grapes. The French breeder François Baco created it by crossing Folle Blanche, the Cognac grape, with a North American riparia vine. It reached New York’s cool-climate vineyards in 1951 and remains a staple of the state’s red wine. It ripens early, keeps a deep color and holds high natural acidity, so it makes vivid, dark, juicy reds even in short northern seasons.

The 2023 shows blackberry and black cherry, with smoke, black pepper and an earthy undertone. Medium-bodied and fresh, it suits grilled and wood-roasted meats. Baco Noir’s high acidity and low tannin give it a juicy, food-friendly profile, a little like a Côtes du Rhône. It is a red with deep roots in Upstate New York, poured here about forty minutes from where it was made.
facts: 100% Baco Noir (Folle Blanche × Vitis riparia hybrid)
North shore of Oneida Lake, Oswego County, New York
